# 佛說呪目經

**ID:** T1328
**Volume:** T21
**Category:** 密教部類
**Original Category:** 密教部
**Byline:** 東晉 曇無蘭譯
**Dynasty:** 東晉
**Date:** 381–395
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1328

## Contributors
- 曇無蘭 (A001788)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The shortest text in this group: a one-paragraph anonymous healing-sūtra of the **early-medieval *zhòujīng* (呪經) cluster**, preserved alongside [KR6j0557](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0557) T1326 (plague), [KR6j0558](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0558) T1327 (toothache), and the related T1329 (infant illness). The four texts share a stylistic profile that places them in the **Eastern-Jìn to Liú-Sòng period** — the same milieu in which the prolific Eastern-Jìn translator [曇無蘭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%98%AD) (Tánwúlán; fl. 381–395) was active. The eye-disease, toothache, and plague triad is one of the most consistent groupings in the canonical *zhòujīng* tradition; the *Kāiyuán shìjiào lù* and other early Táng catalogs treat the three as a single cluster of "small" anonymous translations of the Eastern-Jìn period.

**Abstract**

The text consists, in its entirety, of one transcribed dhāraṇī of nine *pādas* and a one-line application:

> *tuíkòufū bānkòufū / èzhā bānkòufū / jiūlífū / jiūlíbǐfū / jiūluójiūpǐbǐfū / shālísuōpǐbōtífū / yīlífū / yīluóyífū / yīlàbiēfū*
>
> "If the eyes are painful, recite the spell seven times and they will be cured."

The dhāraṇī syllables resist confident Sanskrit reconstruction; their phonological profile (high incidence of *fū* finals, the *jiū-lí / yī-lí* alternation) is consistent with a Prakrit or Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit source mediated through a Central-Asian transcription convention. There is no narrative frame, no *evaṃ mayā śrutam*, no merit-catalogue, no offering instruction. The text is essentially a magical recipe-card, the Eastern-Jin equivalent of an apotropaic charm.

The text is **anonymous** in the catalog tradition. The placement here under the Eastern-Jìn (東晉) dynasty follows the conventional grouping of the Taishō with the demonstrably Eastern-Jìn [KR6j0558](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0558) T1327 ([曇無蘭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%98%AD)) and the parallel anonymous T1326 and T1329; it is plausible but not certain that all three (perhaps four) anonymous *zhòujīng* are likewise products of Tánwúlán's Yángzhōu atelier or of the same milieu. The dating bracket given here (350–500) is appropriately broad.

The text is one of the simplest and most archaic of the Chinese Buddhist eye-disease healing-dhāraṇī, preceding by some four centuries the elaborate Táng Esoteric eye-disease sūtra [KR6j0555](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0555) (T1324) translated by [不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA) Bùkōng. The juxtaposition of the two texts in the same Taishō volume neatly exemplifies the **double tradition** of Chinese Buddhist healing-magic: the early-medieval *zhòujīng* of native-Chinese amulet-and-charm style on the one hand, and the late-Táng Esoteric *vidyā-rāja* dhāraṇī with full Sanskrit-Indic apparatus on the other.
